Japanese gagaku players usually come from a handful of families or institutions that have carried it for a very long time; the training period is extremely long, and they learn instrument, dance and ritual etiquette at the same time. That way of transmitting the music is why the repertoire and the performing details have changed so little over a thousand years.

That is the key difference: a period ensemble has to do the research and reconstruct a way of playing, whereas gagaku's way of playing has simply been handed down. For that reason there is almost no such thing as a "different interpretation" of gagaku, while period-instrument recordings often differ with every conductor.
